prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: مواقيت الصلاة في مدن سعودية (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "المدينة" · longest unbreakable word 49px · one-line width 91px
  col 2: header "الفجر" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 3: header "الظهر" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 4: header "العصر" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 5: header "المغرب" · longest unbreakable word 47px · one-line width 47px
  col 6: header "العشاء" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 414px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 413px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A quick-reference timetable of daily prayer times for six Saudi cities: readers look up one city's day, or compare one prayer across cities.","reading":"Right-to-left: the eye lands on the city name (row header) first, then sweeps left across the five prayer times; the dominant comparison is column-wise (same prayer across cities), with row-wise reading as the secondary mode.","groups":["col 1 (المدينة) is the row identifier and must be visually separated from the data block","cols 2–6 (الفجر، الظهر، العصر، المغرب، العشاء) are five instances of the same kind of value — clock times — and should read as one uniform band, with no column appearing more important than another"],"keep_intact":["every time value, e.g. 8:16, 12:24, 3:23 — they must never wrap or break at the colon","the single-word headers الفجر، الظهر، العصر، المغرب، العشاء, which cannot wrap and set each column's minimum width"],"may_wrap":["city names, especially المدينة المنورة (two words) and مكة المكرمة — wrapping them to a second line is harmless because the row height already accommodates two lines"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [79, 66, 66, 66, 68, 68] · table 414×301px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [72, 68, 68, 68, 68, 69] · table 414×301px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [84, 65, 65, 64, 69, 66] · table 414×301px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r1A","good":"The city column is clearly the widest (79px), so the row identifier separates cleanly from the data block; all six headers stay on one line, no mid-word splits, and the five prayer columns read as a single band.","problems":"The prayer band is uniformly too generous: العشاء carries 68px for a 41px header (27px dead space) and الفجر 66px for 35px, while the city column still cannot hold مكة المكرمة or المدينة المنورة on one line. The two-line city names break into lines of very unequal length, so those two rows look lopsided inside their 60px blocks, and the time figures float in air rather than sitting in a tight band.","cause":"Slack was spent on the short-header prayer columns (66–68px each) instead of on col 1; col 1's 79px (58px content) is 33px short of the 91px needed for one-line city names."},{"design":"r1B","good":"The most regular of the three: every prayer column is 68px, so the five time columns form a perfectly even band, headers unwrapped, and no row looks structurally different from another.","problems":"The hierarchy is inverted: the row identifier is the narrowest-ish column at 72px (51px content) against a 49px longest unbreakable word, leaving ~2px of side margin, so المدينة المنورة nearly touches both cell edges and the wrapped city names look crammed. Meanwhile العشاء (41px needed) sits in 68px of space. The column that a reader uses first is the one that looks squeezed.","cause":"Fixed equal widths of 68–69px for all five prayer columns force col 1 down to the residual 72px, just above the hard 49px word minimum."},{"design":"r1C","good":"The strongest of the three: col 1 gets the most width (84px), and tightening the prayer columns to 65/65/64/69/66 pulls the numbers into a visibly tighter band that reads as one group of like values.","problems":"The slack inside the band is uneven: المغرب at 69px sits only 1px above its 68px minimum, so its header looks pinched against the cell borders, while الفجر and الظهر at 65px each have 9px of air. The eye reads المغرب as cramped and the neighbouring columns as loose, which breaks the uniform band the design is aiming for; the city names still wrap.","cause":"Prayer widths were chosen by eye per column rather than as (column minimum + a constant buffer), so the buffers vary from 1px to 9px."}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"one-line-all","widths":[112,56,56,59,68,62],"change":"Every column gets exactly its measured one-line width (col 1 91+21=112, then 56/56/59/68/62 = the exact minimums of الفجر/الظهر/العصر/المغرب/العشاء). Result: no cell wraps anywhere — المدينة المنورة and مكة المكرمة sit on one line, all seven rows collapse to a uniform 36px height, and the table becomes a compact 252px grid instead of 301px with two 60px rows. Col 1 at 112px also gives the row identifier the visual weight it needs. Slack is zero, so this is the exact-fit design: any 1–2px measurement error in a bold header would cause a wrap."},{"name":"cushion","widths":[102,58,58,61,70,64],"change":"Same minimum-plus-constant-buffer logic but with a 2px buffer on each prayer column (56+2, 56+2, 59+2, 68+2, 62+2) and the remaining 102px to col 1. This removes r1C's 1px pinch on المغرب and its 9px looseness on الفجر/الظهر — all five columns now breathe equally — while col 1 reaches 81px of content, enough for مكة المكرمة on one line and only المدينة المنورة wrapping."},{"name":"even-band","widths":[92,60,60,63,72,66],"change":"A 4px buffer on every prayer column (60/60/63/72/66) makes the band maximally even and comfortable, at the cost of col 1 dropping to 92px (71px content), so the two longest city names wrap to two lines. This is the direct fix of r1C: identical buffers instead of 1–9px variation, a wider city column, and no column that looks pinched."}]}
